name: capability-preflight
what_it_does: Proves in one pass that every system a job needs is really reachable, with a real read and a real write each, before the job starts.
what_you_say: check we can actually reach everything before we start
what_you_get: A pass or fail report per system, and one combined list of what is blocked with the fix for each.
on_your_computer: Runs the shell commands you wrote into a manifest file, which can read, write and delete anything your account can, then prints a pass or fail report. Needs Python.

name: plan-gate
what_it_does: Investigates your project and the live systems a change would touch, then hands back a plan with a goal, up to three questions, numbered assumptions and the files it would change, and stops.
what_you_say: plan this first, don't write any code yet
what_you_get: A written plan in four parts, with each assumption stated so you can disagree with it, and nothing changed.
on_your_computer: Reads your project files and runs look-only cloud and container commands using logins you already have, then hands back a written plan and stops.

name: standing-authorization
what_it_does: Keeps a project file of what Claude Code may already do without asking, what it must always ask about, and the limits on each, and checks a question against it.
what_you_say: set up standing authorization for this project
what_you_get: A starter permissions file, and on any later question a verdict of already granted, must ask, or not covered yet.
on_your_computer: Writes one starter file, and that file then tells Claude it may edit and delete files in the project, run builds, commit, push branches and open pull requests without asking you first, until you cut the list down. Needs Python.

name: output-lint
what_it_does: Checks a message or document you are about to send for six specific faults, such as a command with a blank left in it, or a count with nothing behind it.
what_you_say: lint this before I send it
what_you_get: A list of what it found, with the line, and a footer naming the two things it did not check.
on_your_computer: Runs a small Python program that reads the one draft you point at and prints what it thinks is wrong with it, changing nothing.
